title: Homemade instruments from his youth
summary: As a boy he made trap drums, cymbals and a tube bass from scraps; both men recall the fun of jamming on pots, glasses and trunks.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well, they had to run me down to record because around the point of the 30s, I was doing pretty good and didn't realize it. When I really started out, I started with those little trap drums. I don't know if you know you wasn't born. No, no, no. We used to build our equipment in our hands. Make drums. We'd get to those dying homes and put tissue paper in them and make a kazooka. Yeah.
There's some Dixon and Band here. Yeah. The guy plays a big... Yeah. He's got a kazooka right now.

He's doing well with it. And we used to make those trap drums, we used to get the reels from those moving pitchers, theaters, take the reels out, we didn't make that, we'd make cymbals and snare drums out of the other works. Yeah.
Mm-hmm. Yeah. So, fellas all enjoyed it so well that we started making bass out of a guitar, a string, a tube. Mm-hmm.
We really enjoyed it. Yeah, that's a lot of fun. Oh, it was.
It was more fun than the real music. Yeah.
Yeah. There wasn't a jealousy in it.
Everybody enjoyed, you know, what they created and what they were doing.

Yeah, up at our house, every afternoon, we tried jamming all afternoon, you know. Yeah. Everybody just gets together, we get everybody up there. Yeah, we used to rehearse with glasses and coffee pots and different things. You know, just looking for, searching for sounds and beats and whatnot.

with glasses and cans and whatnot. Yeah. Yeah, our kitchen gets an awful lot of use there. We got, like, at home we got a flat top and somebody's got an electric bass with a little bitty old Princeton amplifier. Yeah. And we got lots of pots and pans and lots of harmonicas and stuff. We make more racket all afternoon. We have a lot more fun doing that than we did playing, you know, music.
